title: console: Settings → Access policy does not show the administrator the client address the server judges (GET /api/v1/auth/client-address)
body:
domain:server#6 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5p3T5YWhLjurajudnQ

Follow-up of #31030 (PR #31258), should-fix S3 of its contract review (6712531628 on PR #31258) and the dev's out-of-scope seam (report 6712418683 on #31030, `carrier: none`), filed by `domain:server#6`. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p2 (the server half exists; without the console half an organization administrator still sets an IP list blind and can lock themselves out of their own organization).

**Business reason.** #31030's point was that an organization administrator can see the address the server judges BEFORE saving an IP allow-list. PR #31258 adds the served read, `GET /api/v1/auth/client-address` (organization administrators with `setup.write`, closed empty query set, `Cache-Control: no-store`, answers the connection's judged address and `trustProxy`). Nothing in the console reads it yet: Settings → Access policy shows no "your current address" hint, so the administrator only learns the address from the save refusal's `constraint.clientAddress`.

**Expected:** the Access policy settings page shows the caller's judged address (and, when `trustProxy` is false behind a proxy, a short note that the address is the proxy's) next to the IP ranges field, read from that route. A failed read leaves the page as today.

Lane: `domain:ui`. Lands after PR #31258.
